h3>One formula in every season

The primary number uses the supplied research’s Tier 3 UTCI fallback with estimated cloud-dependent radiant exposure. It is a weather-exposure estimate, not a claim that a person’s skin is at that temperature, and not calibrated EPST. The radiation-inclusive estimate is not measured sunlight. The Stull approximation is retained for separate wet-bulb context, never added twice.

Every current and forecast value uses matching temperature, dew point or humidity, wind and sky conditions. Sun position changes by location and hour. Direct, diffuse and reflected short-wave radiation are modeled separately; shade blocks direct sun but retains diffuse and reflected radiation. Actual body orientation, clothing, wet skin/clothing, dappled shade and street geometry are not measured.

Long-wave mean radiant temperature is assumed equal to air temperature because surface measurements are unavailable. No fixed urban bonus is applied. Calm wind is evaluated at UTCI’s 0.5 m/s lower bound; out-of-domain inputs stay unavailable. This is not the Fiala/Zhang research-grade implementation or a validated individual thermal-sensation prediction.

UTCI baseline, radiant inputs, shade reference and stress category are retained in the API. The main value includes modeled weather exposure; the illustrated shade reference is labeled separately. Current and future forecasts are not interchangeable observations.

References: UTCI research · pythermalcomfort 4.4.2 numerical implementation. Polynomial attribution: MIT license. Broader uncertainty remains from estimated radiation and spatial mismatch
